threads.body: When `AGENT_RESULT=success` but no `cleanup.patch` is found, this now always creates/pushes an empty commit. Because the workflow’s artifact download/upload steps are `continue-on-error`, a transient artifact issue could also produce “no cleanup.patch” even when the agent actually generated changes, and this would incorrectly record the module as a no-op while still marking it processed (dropping the real patch). Consider gating the empty-commit path on a positive signal that the agent artifact was downloaded correctly (e.g., presence of `agent_output.json` / expected directories), or treat a missing artifact on success as a failure and record it in failed.txt instead of creating the empty commit.

Fixed in https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/commit/1ef55955dee1ffacd9f42d419f795175c2de61fa.

The export step now writes an explicit cleanup.noop marker for intentional no-op runs, and finalize treats a missing cleanup.patch/cleanup.noop result as a failure instead of creating an empty cleanup commit.

threads.body: Now that successful no-op runs add an empty commit to the wip branch, it’s possible for `origin/$WIP_BRANCH` to be ahead of `origin/main` while `FILE_COUNT` stays 0 (only empty commits). When `QUEUE_REMAINING` reaches 0, the flush logic will still try to create a batch branch + PR even though there are no file changes, which can produce a no-op PR (or potentially cause `gh pr create` to fail depending on GitHub’s behavior for empty diffs). Consider preventing flush/PR creation when the wip tree matches main (e.g., require `FILE_COUNT > 0` before flushing, or detect tree equality and just drop the wip branch / skip PR creation).

replies.body:
Fixed in https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/commit/3589d97ca87b18b584d2c60b8fcb18ac74524e3e4.

The flush logic now requires the wip branch to have file changes before creating a batch PR, so a branch containing only empty no-op review commits is skipped instead of producing an empty-diff PR.
